With price currently trading at $1.096, XRP has already recorded another substantial drop. The market positioning of the asset remains weak, as XRP is trading below its major moving averages. Higher lows and fundamental improvements are two main priorities for the asset right now.

XRP's last bullish hope was a short recovery rally towards the $1.34 price threshold. It failed to hold on to that momentum and tumbled towards the area where buyers previously stopped the summer decline. From approximately $1.34, XRP lost roughly 18% of its value and lost everything it built up throughout the recovery.

But where would XRP finally settle down? Realistically, the closest support is the $1.075 level, matching the latest session's low, followed by the $1.03–$1.05 range and the $0.99–$1.00 area, both psychological and technical. Trading activity has also weakened alongside the price. Volume remains substantially below the levels seen during September’s breakout, suggesting that buyers have not yet returned with comparable strength.

Publicly traded Bitcoin mining giant BitFuFu, based in Singapore, has massively increased its Bitcoin holdings in spite of the current crypto market crash.

Bitcoin Treasuries data shows that the Nasdaq-listed mining firm, trading under the ticker FUFU, added 66 BTC to its Bitcoin holdings. This brings the total Bitcoin held by the company to a massive 1,454 BTC.

As per Bitcoin Treasuries data, BitFuFu now ranks 38th in the Bitcoin 100 following the recent increase in its Bitcoin holdings.

BitFuFu’s increase in Bitcoin holdings comes at a time when the overall cryptocurrency market has been hit by a massive sell-off in the past few days.

However, it is worth noting that the rise in Bitcoin holdings by BitFuFu is as of Oct. 31, before the recent increase in selling pressure in the crypto market.

The Singaporean mining firm reported that it had 1,388 BTC in its holdings by the end of September in its operational update dated Nov. 6. This means its Bitcoin holdings in October showed a 4.8% month-over-month increase.

Three consecutive months of increases in Bitcoin holdings by the Singaporean Bitcoin mining giant are evidence that the company is not backing down from increasing its holdings in the top cryptocurrency.

BitFuFu’s latest increase in its Bitcoin holdings comes amid a massive drop in the company’s mining output.

In its latest operational report, BitFuFu reported that it mined 137 BTC in October compared to 167 BTC mined in September. This shows that the company’s mining output decreased by around 18%.

Out of the total 137 BTC mined in October, 67 BTC were mined through self-mining, while 70 BTC were mined through cloud mining.

The reduction in mining output by BitFuFu was mainly due to a huge increase in Bitcoin mining difficulty, which increased by around 11.8% in October.

In October, the total hashrate managed by BitFuFu was 19.5 exahashes per second (EH/s). This is compared to 19.4 EH/s recorded in September.

BitFuFu Chairman and CEO Leo Lu reiterates commitment to increasing Bitcoin holdings.

#5302. Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

Bitcoin CPI reaction: October CPI lands at 8:30 a.m. ET, core seen at 0.22%. Cool prints lifted BTC in the first hour 10 times out of 13.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes October’s consumer price index (CPI) on Tuesday, November 10, at 8:30 a.m. in New York, or 13:30 UTC. The Bitcoin CPI reaction that follows could set the tone for the week. The CPI is the main U.S. measure of inflation, and it will shape the Federal Reserve’s next rate decision.

Economists expect core prices, which leave out food and energy, to have risen about 0.22% in the month. That would be a slowdown from September’s 0.33%.

Economists expect growth in the core CPI to have moderated in October to around 0.22%, though the full range of estimates is broad enough to round down to 0.1% or round up to 0.3%.

Due to the government shutdown in Oct 2025, there's no tidy year-earlier figure. pic.twitter.com/CFM7ikw8fO

— Nick Timiraos (@NickTimiraos) November 9, 2026

Bitcoin trades near $74,400, still close to Sunday’s two-month low of $73,510.

CPI days move crypto. We checked Bitcoin’s first hour after the last 24 releases. When core inflation came in at 0.2% or lower, BTC rose in that hour 10 times out of 13. When it came in at 0.3% or higher, it rose only 4 times out of 10.

So which way will today’s number push Bitcoin?

The forecasts point to a calmer month. Seventeen banks and research firms surveyed by The Wall Street Journal see a median rise of 0.25% for headline CPI and 0.22% for core. Journal reporter Nick Timiraos posted the table on X.

That spread matters. The government reports CPI rounded to one decimal place. With forecasts this spread out, the core reading could print anywhere from 0.1% to 0.3%. A 0.3% would match September’s pace and read as inflation that is not cooling.

The yearly comparison will also be messy. The government shutdown in October 2025 meant no CPI was published for that month, so there is no clean year-over-year figure.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

This is the last CPI report the Federal Reserve will see before its December 8-9 meeting. Traders already expect a rate hike: on Tuesday morning, Polymarket gives an 86.5% chance of a 0.25-point increase and 11.5% for no change.

Higher rates tend to weigh on Bitcoin. They make cash and bonds pay more, which pulls money away from assets that pay no interest, like crypto.

A cool reading could shave those odds and give Bitcoin room to bounce. A hot one would lock in the hike.

DISCOVER: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

We measured the Bitcoin CPI reaction on Binance. We took the 24 CPI reports published since October 2024 and measured Bitcoin’s move in the hour after each 8:30 a.m. release.

The pattern is a lean, not a rule. The biggest drop came on February 12, 2025, when core rose 0.4% and BTC lost 1.9% in an hour. Last month’s 0.3% reading cost it 1.4%.

So far it has. BTC trades at $74,398 on Binance, about 1.2% above Sunday’s low.

On the daily chart, Bitcoin sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that weight recent prices more. The 200-day EMA is at $76,481 and the 50-day EMA at $79,128.

For anyone tracking the Bitcoin CPI reaction, the first hour after 8:30 a.m. is the one to watch. In 20 of the last 24 reports, Bitcoin ended the next 24 hours moving in the same direction as in that first hour.

#5301. How Bittensor's Gamma Turns Every AI Payment Into an Alpha Burn

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Paying a Bittensor subnet with gamma burns its alpha token. Here is how gamma gets minted, how the lower-price rule works and why the credit can never be converted back.Pay a Bittensor subnet for an AI answer with gamma, and your payment vanishes. The alpha token behind it gets burned, the credit gets spent, and nobody can redeem either one.

Using a subnet's service today usually means creating an account, adding funds and collecting an API key, and every additional subnet repeats the routine. Opentensor announced gamma to cut that friction. With gamma, a Bittensor wallet handles both access and payment across any subnet that adopts the standard.The mechanics are laid out in the gamma guide in the subtensor docs. Gamma is a credit a subnet can accept as payment, valued in US dollars. A customer gets it by burning that subnet's alpha token, and each dollar of burned alpha value mints one gamma, so a burn valued at $100 creates 100 gamma.Each balance stays tied to the subnet where it was created. Gamma minted for subnet 51 can't pay for a service on any other subnet. Root switches the system on network-wide, and each subnet owner or lease beneficiary then enables it for their own subnet.

Customers have two ways in. They can pay with TAO, and the protocol buys the subnet’s alpha and burns it in a single transaction. Or they can pay with alpha they already hold on that subnet, and the protocol burns it directly to create gamma.

Setup takes four steps. The customer creates a fresh hotkey that will act as an API key, associates it with their coldkey, looks up the service they want and mints. The docs give the command: btcli gamma mint --netuid 51 --hotkey API_KEY --amount-tao 10 --service-hotkey SERVICE_HOTKEY. The TAO route follows the same pool and flow accounting as stake-burn and creates no stake position. Users who hold stake can burn it with mint-gamma-with-stake, and --amount-alpha all burns the whole position.

The gamma lands in a deposit. Each deposit belongs to the minting coldkey and is keyed by the API-key hotkey, which signs the customer's requests. A hotkey holds at most one deposit per subnet, and a coldkey holds at most 64 per subnet. The docs warn against reusing a staking hotkey or a coldkey, because requests signed with the key get paid from the deposit.A few guardrails apply. A mint must reach at least 0.1 gamma. By default, the SDK quotes the mint first and fails it if the result lands more than 5% below the quote. The mint also needs a TAO/USD price no older than 300 blocks, about an hour.

Gamma’s valuation rule decides how much credit a burn buys. The protocol values the burned alpha in TAO, then converts that figure to dollars through an on-chain TAO/USD price feed. The TAO value equals alpha multiplied by the lower of two prices, the gamma price and the spot price, which the docs write as alpha × min(gamma price, spot price).

Every subnet keeps a gamma price. When a subnet registers, the price starts at the median alpha price across subnets. After that it moves asymmetrically. If spot falls, the gamma price falls to match at once. If spot rises, the gamma price climbs slowly toward it, closing a small slice of the gap each block, so the gap halves every 600 blocks, roughly two hours. However high spot jumps, the gamma price can at most double every 600 blocks.An example shows the effect. Say a user burns 100 alpha when spot sits at 0.05 TAO but the gamma price lags at 0.04. The mint uses 0.04, which gives 4 TAO of value, and at $400 per TAO that mints 1,600 gamma. Had the gamma price caught up, the same burn would mint 2,000, so the lag costs the burner 400 gamma. A short-lived pump buys no extra credit. The figures are illustrative, but the rule comes straight from the docs.The TAO/USD feed gets similar damping. A root-controlled oracle supplies the price, and the accepted price falls to a lower feed immediately but rises at most 66 parts per million per block, about 2% an hour. The docs admit the oracle is trusted: its accepted price can climb up to roughly 61% a day until root replaces or removes it.One more detail matters. The docs say alpha is valued at these prices, not at what selling it would return, so a burn that is large relative to the pool is worth more than a sale would be. A big burner gets credit for full value instead of a slipped sale price.Once minted, gamma holds its dollar value whether TAO or alpha prices rise or fall. Service providers still set their own prices.

To use a service, a person or an AI agent signs a request with a hotkey from their Bittensor wallet. The subnet owner, or another authorized account, deducts the required credits from that hotkey's gamma balance before delivering the service. Nothing transfers to anyone. The designated spender calls `spend-gamma` with up to 512 entries per call, each naming a hotkey, an amount and a 32-byte reference, and the spent gamma is destroyed on the spot.The reference doubles as a receipt. By convention it holds the service's own ID for the request being paid, returned with the response, so the customer can match each spend to a specific request. The chain repeats the reference in its events and reads it nowhere else, so an entry sent twice spends twice.Customers keep control throughout. The minting coldkey can set a daily spend cap that refills linearly over 7,200 blocks, about a day, and a cap of zero pauses the deposit. The coldkey can also change the spender, keep separate deposits for different apps and agents, and top up an existing deposit without switching hotkeys. Because the coldkey can pause or redirect at any moment, services spend ahead: they spend what they are about to serve, then serve what was spent. A spender can hand this right to a `GammaSpend` proxy, which can make no other call.Both minting and spending leave public records on-chain, so anyone can audit how much credit a subnet has created and how much customers have used.

The limits are strict. Gamma can't be transferred to another wallet, and it can't be converted back into alpha or TAO. It confers no claim on any party and can't be redeemed. Each subnet chooses whether, and at what prices, it accepts its own gamma.

The docs flag the sharpest risk directly: dissolving or pruning a subnet destroys all of its gamma, and holders receive nothing. A customer who prepaid a large deposit to a subnet that later shuts down loses it. Moving gamma between your own deposits is allowed, and a deposit opened under someone else's hotkey stays yours, since you can pull the gamma back at any time.A coldkey swap adds a few wrinkles. While one is announced, the coldkey's gamma calls are refused, though its spenders keep spending. After a subnet owner swaps coldkeys, deposits that name the old one keep it until the owner republishes its service.

The docs answer the economic question in one sentence: spent gamma pays its spender nothing. The value of the burned alpha accrues to the subnet's alpha holders.

That makes gamma a direct demand mechanism for alpha. Creating gamma always burns the subnet's alpha, which removes those tokens from circulation for good. When customers pay with TAO, the protocol first buys alpha from the subnet's pool, so TAO-funded purchases add buying pressure before the burn. Every dollar of AI usage ties a purchase of service credits to a burn of alpha.

A service operator earns through the alpha it holds and the emissions its subnet receives, not through a payment from customers. The structure rewards subnets that attract real usage, since usage shrinks their alpha supply.Two questions remain open. Customers get dollar-denominated credit, but the burn that funds it follows alpha prices, so heavy usage during a price spike may feel expensive. Holders also carry the dissolution risk, which will push careful buyers toward established subnets. Which services accept gamma, and at what price, will show whether this becomes a real payments layer or a niche tool. The mechanism is clear, and adoption is the unknown.

According to Glassnode’s latest Weekly Market Pulse report, Bitcoin was trading around $75,000 on Monday after a turbulent week that saw the leading cryptocurrency briefly push above $80,000 before rapidly giving back those gains. The price closed more than 4% lower than the previous Sunday and marked its weakest finish since August.

The midweek rally above $80,000 reversed the very next day, and selling resumed over the weekend, with ETF investors playing a clear role in the pressure. Glassnode data shows the funds posted outflows on four of five trading days, delivering the heaviest weekly total since early July. ETF MVRV has now slipped below its lower band, indicating that the profit cushion for these holders is thinning.

Derivatives markets reflected caution rather than full capitulation, with perpetual futures traders sold aggressively into Thursday’s drop and again on Sunday as long liquidations rose.

Open interest, however, remains in the upper part of its range, and long positions continue to pay elevated funding rates. Options traders are still paying for protection, with the 25-delta skew above its high band, even as the volatility spread retreated into its normal range once realized moves caught up.

Spot buyers failed to step in meaningfully, and cumulative volume delta turned negative despite rising volume. Notably, on-chain activity told a similar story of repositioning, with transfer volumes and active addresses both climbing above their upper bands while fees increased, Glassnode noted.

Supply has continued to shift into newer hands, as the short-term-to-long-term holder supply ratio and the share of hot capital remain elevated. Short-term holders now sit near break-even, and realized losses clearly outweigh profits.

The combination of persistent ETF selling and fragile short-term holder positions is weighing on price. At the same time, some leverage has been flushed from the system, and recent momentum no longer strongly supports further downside. Traders are now actively watching to see whether the market can stabilize or if another leg lower is still ahead.

#5298. Critical Ethereum Security Alert Issued Over Compromised Software

Blockchain security provider SlowMist has issued an urgent security alert for Ethereum ecosystem users after a complex supply chain attack was detected on Ethersphere's software.

In a recent post on the X social media platform, SlowMist announced that two pieces of software have been compromised by hackers.

The cybersecurity firm claims that attackers were able to break into GitHub accounts and take advantage of legitimate software release processes to deploy malicious software.

The attack could potentially impact users on multiple operating systems, including Windows, macOS and Linux.

The affected software is part of Swarm, a decentralized storage network belonging to the wider Ethereum ecosystem.

Security experts have cautioned that these malicious software releases could enable attackers to compromise cryptocurrency wallet credentials, steal private keys and open up permanent backdoors on affected systems.

One of the most concerning features of this attack is the involvement of Ethereum's blockchain infrastructure in helping manage the malicious software.

SlowMist explains that this malware retrieves and runs malicious JavaScript code.

However, this attack is not just a simple malware infection.

The cybersecurity firm disclosed that attackers are leveraging an Ethereum smart contract as a decentralized command-and-control (C2) configuration repository.

This gives attackers the ability to dynamically update server addresses managing the malware without requiring a new deployment of the malicious software.

Interestingly, the same Ethereum smart contract was previously associated with the infamous SleepyDuck and EtherDuck malware attacks. These campaigns targeted developers using malicious extensions on the Open VSX marketplace.

This points to the possibility that the new attack may be part of a broader operation aimed at compromising cryptocurrency developers and users.

Independent security researchers from Socket and SafeDep also discovered malware aimed at stealing Swarm wallet files and deploying persistent remote access tools.

As a result of this discovery, SlowMist advised users to immediately uninstall the affected package and roll back to the clean version 13.2.0.

In the meantime, users of Swarm Desktop v0.56.2 were advised to update to the clean v0.56.3 software release.

#5295. XRP Price Plunges to $1.05 After a Hot CPI Report: Will the Support Stand?

Ripple XRP fell to $1.05 after a hot CPI report. After 7 of the last 10 hot reports, XRP was higher a day later. Can $1.05 hold?

Ripple XRP fell to $1.05 on Tuesday within five minutes of the U.S. October consumer price index (CPI) report, which showed XRP USD price rising faster than economists expected.

XRP crypto traded at $1.0797 when the report came out at 8:30 a.m. in New York, or 13:30 UTC. By 13:35 UTC it had touched $1.0500 on Binance, a 2.8% drop and its lowest price since August 19. It has since bounced to about $1.07. Bitcoin fell with it, dropping to $73,525 in the same five minutes.

The drop puts XRP back on a level it has tested before. Between late June and mid-August, XRP traded around $1.05 for weeks. The level held the first time and broke the second.

So will the support stand this time, and what do the CPI numbers tell us?

BREAKING: October CPI inflation rises +0.4% month-over-month, above expectations of +0.3%.

Core CPI inflation rose +0.3%, also above expectations of +0.2%.

BLS will not be releasing year-over-year figures due to the October 2025 government shutdown.

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 10, 2026

Prices rose faster than forecast in October. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in the month, against the 0.3% economists expected.

Core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. The forecast was 0.2%. Core inflation has now run at about 0.3% for three months in a row.

The report is missing one usual figure. The bureau did not publish a yearly inflation rate because it never collected prices in October 2025, during the government shutdown. That leaves the monthly numbers to carry the whole report.

Those monthly numbers matter for the Federal Reserve. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech this morning that he already leans toward a 0.25 percentage point rate hike in December. If core CPI came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 0.5 point hike “should be considered”.

Core CPI did come in at 0.3%. Before the release, traders saw almost no chance of a hike that large. Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money out of risky assets like XRP.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The first move after a hot report has often faded. We measured XRP’s price on Binance in the 24 hours after each of the last 24 CPI reports, from October 2024 to October 2026.

Ten of those reports had core inflation of 0.3% or higher, like today’s. After seven of them, XRP was higher 24 hours later. The median move was a 1.4% gain.

The record is weaker this year. Of the four hot reports in 2026, XRP was higher a day later only twice. After the last one, on October 14, it fell 4.4% in 24 hours.

The difference this time is the Fed. A hot report that only confirms a small hike is easier for traders to shrug off. One that puts a larger hike on the table, as Waller laid out, gives sellers more to work with.

EXPLORE: XRP Price Forecast: Ripple at Risk of Losing Key Support, $1 Next?

The level has a history this year. XRP has spent two long stretches around $1.05 since June.

Today’s low of $1.0500 sits right on that zone. The first test of a level often holds. Each new test tends to leave fewer buyers there.

XRP trades at about $1.07 on Binance after the CPI drop, down 2.8% in 24 hours and 17% in a week. It is 71% below its July 2025 record of $3.65.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, XRP sits well below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA stands at $1.294 and the 200-day EMA at $1.350.

For Ripple XRP, the first test of $1.05 has held so far. The daily close decides it: a close above $1.05 keeps the support alive, while a close below it opens the way to $1.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Top Solana Meme Coins to Bid

Management expects fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $17 billion, plus or minus $300 million. CEO Lisa Su also expects overall revenue growth to exceed 80% in 2027. These figures strengthen AMD’s position in the AI infrastructure market. The next challenge is execution: converting rising demand into larger market share and sustained profitability.

AMD stock trades at $582.05 on November 12, gaining 5.27% during the session. The price chart shows a strong rebound after the stock briefly dropped toward $420–$450 earlier in November. Buyers have pushed shares back above the short- and medium-term moving averages near $510–$534, improving the near-term technical structure.

The immediate resistance zone sits between $650 and $680, where previous rallies encountered selling pressure. A sustained breakout above $680 could open the way toward $700. On the downside, $550 is the first support area, followed by $534 and $510. A decline below $510 would weaken the recovery and bring the longer-term support near $442 into focus.

Nvidia’s leadership transition has created an opportunity for AMD, but the semiconductor market will not change overnight. Customers must qualify alternative processors, adapt their software infrastructure and establish new supply arrangements before shifting large workloads.

AMD already has a growing data-center business, an expanding Instinct GPU portfolio and strong demand for EPYC processors. These fundamentals give the company a credible opportunity to compete for a larger share of AI infrastructure spending.

The real test for AMD is whether it can turn the current investor interest into lasting customer demand. A move above $650 would strengthen the bullish chart, but sustained revenue and market-share growth will ultimately determine the stock’s next leg.

#5292. XRP Ledger Testnet and Devnet Face Major November Reset Wiping All Data

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. XRP ledger developers have been notified regarding upcoming resets for Testnet and Devnets. According to a statement, XRPL testnet and devnet are scheduled for a reset on November 25, 2026, to improve full history server stability.

Testnet and Devnet for XRP Ledger developers will be reset on Nov 25, 2026 at 5–6 PM PT. All on-chain state (accounts, tokens, AMMs, etc.) will be deleted and will need a re-fund and re-setup afterward. Other networks will continue to operate as usual, including Mainnet, Xahau, and the Hooks Testnet.

Ripple runs Testnet and Devnet, so the community can test out new features and integrations without risking real money.

The XRPL Testnet used to depend on a single full history server, which went down and cannot be recovered without a reset. To avoid this from happening again, an upgrade was performed to increase the server storage capacity.

The resets will delete all ledger data in Testnet and Devnet, including all accounts, transactions, balances, settings, offers, AMMs, escrows, and other data. Testnet will have its Amendment statuses restored to match Mainnet's. However, any AMMs that are re-created after the reset will generally have different account addresses. As a best practice, users are urged not to use the same addresses or key pairs on Mainnet and any test networks.

The important URLs, Network ID, and validator settings for both the devnet and testnets will stay the same. For XRPL users who run an xrpld server that is connected to testnet or Devnet, after the reset they should delete their database data and restart the server.

The last time the XRPL devnet saw a reset was on March 3, 2026. This was necessitated due to the Batch amendment, which required more development at the time and to prevent validators from becoming amendment-blocked, a Devnet reset was required.

The XRPL foundation has launched the XRP Ledger Education Month with up to $40,000 in awards for educators and content creators who explain upcoming amendments like the Lending Protocol or teach how the XRP Ledger works, the role of XRP and the core protocol philosophies.

Since XRPL 3.3.0, memory consumption has been reduced by up to 23% on nodes. Memory growth in XRPL nodes was observed in late summer 2025 and a fix shipped in xrpld 3.3.0.

#5290. XRP Ledger Introduces Quantum-Proof Security Upgrade to Users

As the XRP Ledger developers continue to make committed efforts to make the network fully quantum-resistant in the coming year, the team has just proposed a major upgrade that has sparked a buzz across the XRP community.

Sparking fresh excitement across the XRP community earlier today, the XRP Ledger (XRPL) Foundation has disclosed plans to introduce quantum-resistant accounts to users.

The team revealed plans to introduce a new feature to the XRP Ledger to offer users strict protection against future quantum computing threats without paying additional transaction fees.

While it is yet to be implemented, the proposed design will allow users to add a NIST-approved ML-DSA-44 signing key to their accounts and disable their existing keys.

This way, it will become harder for potential quantum attacks to compromise accounts, especially those whose public keys have already been exposed.

Apart from the extra layer of protection the upgrade promises to offer users, its cost-effective design has stirred more interest among the XRP community.

Notably, users will not have to pay higher transaction fees to access the additional security, as the proposed feature allows XRP holders to strengthen their account protection without worrying about extra transaction costs.

The proposed upgrade sends relief across the crypto ecosystem as it addresses concerns about the possibility of increasingly powerful quantum computers eventually breaking some of the cryptographic systems currently used to secure blockchains and cryptocurrencies.

While the upgrade is yet to launch, the team revealed that it has scheduled a migration study for the first half of 2027.

The study is aimed at examining how existing accounts can transition to the new security system and what the process would involve for users.

The proposed security upgrade has further sparked more optimism as it is also part of Ripple's broader aim of achieving full quantum protection by 2028.

#5285. Binance Shuts Down Transfers Involving MEXC and Its Affiliates

Just a few days after the U.S. Treasury took action to cut global crypto exchange MEXC off from the U.S. financial system, Binance has also announced strict regulatory actions against the exchange.

On Tuesday, November 10, Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, announced its immediate decision to halt all transfers involving MEXC and all its affiliated companies.

Binance released an official announcement earlier today, warning users that it has stopped all trading services related to MEXC following new concerns about its legitimacy.

While the restrictions were announced to take effect immediately, Binance explained that its move follows the recent decision by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) to designate MEXC as a Primary Money Laundering Concern.

As such, Binance has prohibited its users from directly or indirectly sending funds to, receiving funds from, or conducting transactions through Binance involving MEXC and its related entities.

The MEXC-affiliated entities mentioned by Binance include MEXC Global Limited, MEXC Estonia OÜ, MEXC Singapore Pte Ltd, MEXC Global Foundation Ltd, GIDA Technology AG, and several other companies and affiliates operating under the MEXC name.

Although MEXC is among the top 20 crypto exchanges in the world, FinCEN issued an order against MEXC on November 6, cutting the exchange off from the U.S. financial system amid recent fraud allegations.

Notably, the U.S. Treasury accused the exchange of facilitating at least $16 billion in illicit transactions tied to sanctions evasion and cybercrime and of defrauding people of their funds.

While Binance remains the first crypto exchange to take action in accordance with FinCEN’s rule, it appears that many other exchanges are lining up to take similar action.

#5284. Why Is Crypto Crashing Today? Bitcoin Falls Below $73K as Zcash (ZEC) Leads Crypto Losses

Why is crypto crashing? A hot CPI report raised Fed hike bets. ZEC fell below $1,000, the worst of 20 large coins this week.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

Trader 0x8742 opened a 10x long on 18,000 $ZEC ($17.63M) and is now down over $2.8M.

Liquidation price: $895.46.https://t.co/azzt3xvmay pic.twitter.com/wczndt7doC

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 11, 2026

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

Inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

That reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

When markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

Sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

EXPLORE: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

ZEC trades at about $966. It touched $961.07 on Wednesday, its lowest price since September 4.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, ZEC has fallen below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1,200.68. It is still above its 200-day EMA at $872.23.

For Bitcoin, the line to watch is Tuesday’s low of $72,727. Below that, $68,902, the August 20 low, is the next support.

#5283. Shiba Inu (SHIB) Scammers Fake 'Ryoshi' to Push 137 Scam Tokens and Dupe Investors

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. According to longtime SHIB community member Mazrael, since the SHIB deployer wallet went silent in October 2021, at least 137 scam tokens have falsely claimed that the SHIB deployer sent them the coins. The intent of scammers is to 'fake' Shiba Inu's pseudonymous founder, "Ryoshi," and the reason behind this is to appear legitimate: If "Ryoshi" sent it, people trust it.

Mazrael explains how this trick works: a token is just a program, and it keeps its own record of transfers. The scammer can write any address into that record as the sender. So these scammers write the SHIB deployer's address, and on Etherscan it looks like "Ryoshi" sent the token. However, the real SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021.

How scammers fake "Ryoshi" Since the SHIB deployer wallet went silent in October 2021, at least 137 scam tokens have pretended it sent them their coins. Why? To look legitimate. If "Ryoshi" sent it, people trust it. How the trick works: A token is just a program, and it keeps its own record of transfers. The scammer can write ANY address into that record as the sender. So they write the SHIB deployer's address, and on Etherscan it looks like "Ryoshi" sent you their token. But the deployer never signed anything. Click the transaction itself and look at "From". That's the wallet that really sent it, and it's never the SHIB deployer. The numbers: - 9,131+ fake transfers - 2,500+ wallets hit - 0 signed by the deployer Some of the fakes: APE, three "SHIBA INU2.0" tokens, ShibChain, SHIB DAO, METARUFFY, a token literally called "Ryoshi", Caw and Baby Caw, three fake "Shibarium" tokens (a year before the real one), "BONE2.0" and three "UNLEASHED DAO" tokens. Many got shilled by OGs and ex-admins as "Ryoshi-backed" to make them look legit. The real SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021. Always check who signed the transaction, not what the token says.

'The SHIB deployer never signed anything,' Mazrael stated, urging the crypto community to click on related token transactions and examine the "From" address, saying this is the wallet that sent it and was never the SHIB deployer.

Mazrael shared the numbers, outlining over 9,131 fake transfers, over 2,500 wallets hit, and zero signed by the SHIB deployer. He went on to name some of these fake tokens, adding that some of these tokens got promoted as "Ryoshi-backed" to make them look legitimate.

This disclosure warns crypto users to always check who signed the transaction, not what the token says.

In a separate post, Mazrael explained that nothing links the SHIB deployer address to any person.

The SHIB deployer (0xB8f2…FA08) only deployed one contract: SHIB, and it hasn't sent a single transaction since October 2021. It has no public signed message on record, either on-chain or on Etherscan.

LEASH, BONE, and TREAT each came from different deployers. Mazrael indicated that BONE's deployer is shiba-swap.eth, whereas LEASH came from '0xA221…1494,' the same key that deployed StarLink, whose own site names Woof Decentra as LEASH's developer. That key kept LEASH's rebase oracle, an admin key, for five years.

#5282. Solana Lands Major Wall Street Boost as DTCC Targets 2027 Launch of Tokenized Assets: What It Means for SOL

Wall Street is taking another major step toward blockchain adoption, and Solana (SOL) is emerging as one of the networks positioned to benefit. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the financial infrastructure giant that clears and settles much of the U.S. securities market, plans to bring its tokenization services to Solana in 2027.

The move could open the door to tokenized stocks, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and U.S. Treasuries on the blockchain, marking a significant institutional milestone for Solana. But beyond the headline announcement, the obvious question is what this development could mean for the price of SOL and its long-term investment appeal.

DTCC announced Thursday that it plans to extend its tokenization services to Solana in the second half of 2027. The initiative will connect its DTCC Tokenization Service to the Layer 1 blockchain, enabling eligible securities held by its Depository Trust Company subsidiary to be represented as digital tokens.

BREAKING: @The_DTCC to tokenize custodied assets on Solana. announced plans to connect the DTCC Tokenization Service to Solana, enabling the tokenization of eligible DTC-custodied assets on the network.The integration is planned for the second half of 2027, further advancing… pic.twitter.com/gXszWFgUOX

“DTC-tokenized assets made available on Solana – and all blockchain networks integrated with the service – will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities,” Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services, said in the announcement.

DTCC’s Tokenization Service went live on October 28, initially operating on the Canton Network and the corporation’s own private blockchain, which is built on the Besu framework. The platform allows eligible participants to convert traditional securities into tokenized assets and redeem them back into their original form, with the digital tokens delivered directly to wallets of their choice. At launch, DTCC also outlined plans to expand its tokenization service to additional blockchain networks in 2027, with Stellar and Circle’s Arc among the platforms also slated for integration.

Solana has been stepping up efforts to attract traditional financial institutions, positioning itself as a blockchain capable of supporting large-scale financial activity. Nick Ducoff, head of institutional growth at the Solana Foundation, recently highlighted this appeal, stating that institutions choose Solana because it already “runs real financial activity at scale.” He added that firms are already issuing assets, settling transactions, and deploying capital on the network, according to a post shared by Solana’s official X account.

The potential opportunity becomes clearer when considering DTCC’s position in the U.S. financial system. Through its Depository Trust Company (DTC) subsidiary, the financial infrastructure giant holds approximately $114 trillion in securities on behalf of banks and brokerage firms. Its newly launched tokenization service initially covered 34 eligible securities representing an estimated $30 trillion in potential tokenized assets. However, this figure reflects the value of securities eligible for tokenization, not assets already issued or circulating on blockchain networks.

Bringing even a fraction of this enormous securities market onto Solana could translate into substantial institutional activity and settlement volumes over time. This could create additional opportunities for SOL demand if the token is required for relevant network transactions. Nevertheless, the integration is not expected until the second half of 2027, making the development a potential long-term growth driver rather than an immediate price catalyst. Its ultimate impact will depend on institutional adoption, actual transaction volumes, and whether increased network activity translates into meaningful demand for SOL.

#5280. Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

The bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

Traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third…

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

Following the disbandment of the T3 FCU, TRON and Tether have launched a new initiative to tackle criminal activity in USDT on Tron.

Tron and Tether have formed a strategic partnership with blockchain intelligence platform Chainalysis. The coalition aims to crack down on criminal activity involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the Tron blockchain, according to data Tron CEO Justin Sun shared today.

In a Thursday announcement, Tron, Tether, and Chainalysis formed a digital crime task force (DCTF), a new initiative designed to effectively uncover and clamp down on illicit activity involving USDT on the TRON network.

The DCTF brings together three industry leaders – a stablecoin issuer, a crypto network, and a blockchain intelligence firm – aimed at building investigative capability, with support from global law enforcement authorities. The key driver behind the collaboration is to better combat illegal USDT transactions on Tron amid a surge in AI-enabled crime.

The DCTF takes effect after the T3 Financial Crime Unit (T3 FCU), formed by Tether, Tron, and TRM Labs, ended its role in August. The T3 FCU program, which was rolled out in September 2024, was tasked with disrupting unlawful USDT activity on Tron. Its track record has been good. By mid-2025, it had blocked around $250 million in illicit USDT assets, and by May 2026, it had also frozen over $450 million. It had collaborated with law enforcement agencies in 23 jurisdictions.

In the new announcement issued today, Tether and Tron have launched a new initiative to make the crackdown more efficient with Chainalysis’ support. With the recent massive Binance hack, the timing of the fresh partnership is critical.

The Binance exploit highlights serious security risks for crypto platforms. Reports indicate that the hacker sold around $325 million USDT to market makers within minutes of obtaining the stolen funds.

The formation of the DCTF aims to swiftly unearth and dismantle illegal USDT transactions on Tron. With swift responses and coordination among the parties, the alliance seeks to minimize the time between uncovering criminal activity and freezing assets, particularly as AI-assisted crimes are on the increase.

#5275. Don’t Store Crypto on iPhone, Ledger CTO Says

Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet has recently warned cryptocurrency holders not to store critical wallet information on their iPhones, as the security threat is on the rise.

In his recent post on X, the Ledger executive highlighted the fact that vulnerabilities that can leak important data are now becoming more and more accessible for hackers to exploit.

"Unfortunately this kind of vulnerability used to be very expensive and reserved to high potential attackers," Guillemet tweeted.

However, he pointed out that we're now on the verge of seeing the costs of such vulnerabilities go down to zero, meaning that it could become very easy for cybercriminals to exploit them on a massive scale.

"Simply don't store any valuable in your mobile. Especially not your crypto seeds," the Ledger CTO cautioned.

His words came in response to an urgent security alert published by crypto exchange Binance over a vulnerability that was found in Apple's iOS operating system.

In particular, cryptocurrency exchange Binance reported a vulnerability, dubbed worse_query, which can allow malicious applications to gain access to files of other applications installed on the same device.

As specified by the exchange, this security flaw affects iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1 and 27.2.

This means that crypto wallet recovery phrases, private keys and login credentials can be at risk, as they may be stored in accessible local files.

Binance underscored that this concern isn't exclusive to the exchange's app alone, while adding that the vulnerability can have an impact on the entire crypto space.

The exchange recommended that users uninstall apps that were downloaded from untrusted sources, update their operating systems and avoid installing any unauthorized software.

Binance also advised users to transfer their funds to newly created wallets on clean devices if they think their wallets may have been compromised.

Apple published new security updates on Nov. 9. However, it's not clear if they are enough to fully patch this vulnerability. Still, there have been no confirmed crypto thefts specifically linked to the exploit.

Guillemet's warning comes a month after Ledger's major security incident involving compromised hardware wallets.

Back in October, French cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Ledger admitted that some hardware wallets distributed by its Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis had been tampered with.

It turned out that hackers managed to install complex hardware implants in legitimate Ledger devices. With that, hackers were able to intercept users' recovery phrases when people were setting up their Ledger wallets for the first time.

As shown by Ledger's investigation, malicious implants were capable of capturing the 24-word recovery phrase that appears on the Ledger device screen and then passing it to attackers via a cellular connection.

Blockchain sleuths estimated that this incident might have led to more than $86 million in crypto losses. However, Ledger itself didn't confirm the total amount.

Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO, ticker ANT, is set to price in a $70–$78 range and begin trading on Nasdaq around mid-to-late November 2026, with a targeted valuation as high as $1.4 trillion. However, in a wild turn of events, Anthropic’s own Claude AI predicts that its own share price could tank upon launch.

Yet in an over-the-top bearish scenario, the stock could suffer one of the most dramatic post-IPO collapses in modern market history by January 1, 2027. The landmark catalyst that unlocks this downside is a highly unlikely but not impossible convergence of events: a high-profile safety incident or regulatory action involving Claude models coincides with the deepening fallout from the Nvidia CEO scandal and a broader political backlash against frontier AI.

In this hypothetical, revelations of serious alignment failures or misuse cases trigger emergency congressional hearings, restrictive new rules from multiple governments, and a sudden freeze in enterprise adoption. Combined with already fragile sentiment around massive AI infrastructure spending, the narrative flips from “indispensable technology” to “overhyped liability,” prompting a rapid and severe derating of the entire sector.

(SOURCE: Claude AI Predicts a Disastrous Anthropic IPO)

Because ANT has not yet begun trading, pure technical analysis is necessarily forward-looking. In the bearish path, the stock would open with an initial pop or modest premium but quickly form a series of lower highs as institutional sellers and lock-up-related supply emerge.

A failure to hold the IPO price range as support, followed by a break below key psychological levels such as $60 and then $50, would confirm a distribution pattern. Volume spikes on down days, deteriorating relative strength versus the Nasdaq, and a rapid slide into oversold RSI territory would support the case for further downside, especially if the broader AI complex continues to de-rate.

Anthropic’s seven cofounders each plan to sell approximately $250 million in shares through the company’s IPO $ANT @soberlook @WSJ https://t.co/EGLX7QmA3x pic.twitter.com/FodDa4zUWC

— Mike Zaccardi, CFA, CMT (@MikeZaccardi) November 11, 2026

Measured-move projections from an IPO-range breakdown could theoretically point toward substantially lower levels as the market reassesses growth assumptions under a more hostile regulatory and sentiment regime.

While Anthropic’s revenue growth remains impressive and its strategic backers are formidable, the timing of the listing amid AI-sector turbulence, the Nvidia controversy, and rising negative press creates a fragile backdrop.

An extreme safety or regulatory shock layered on top of that environment could produce the kind of violent repricing rarely seen in large-cap technology debuts.

Anthropic is launching its IPO into a market where AI stocks have been hit hard. Nvidia, a cornerstone investor in the concurrent $26 billion private placement, has seen its shares tumble amid an escalating scandal involving CEO Jensen Huang.

Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, internal investigations, FBI scrutiny, and reports of potential national-security implications.

Broader negative press around AI has intensified, with investors questioning valuation sustainability, capital intensity, and regulatory risk just as Anthropic seeks one of the largest public offerings on record.

The company itself has dialed back earlier whispers of a $2 trillion valuation to the current $70–$78 range amid the cooler climate.

Claude AI predicts that ANT could trade down to the $18–$25 range by January 1, 2027. This is an extremely telling call, considering Claude is Anthropic’s own AI model.

This remains a highly speculative, over-the-top outlook rather than a base-case forecast. The catalyst would require a fundamental shift in how AI infrastructure and autonomous systems settle value, something that is currently a long shot.

#5273. Altcoins Lose an Estimated $200B in Market Cap—Analysts Share Mixed Sentiments

The brief surge in altcoin prices has faded quickly, according to analysis shared by crypto analyst Darkfost. Altcoin market capitalization, excluding Bitcoin and stablecoins, climbed by $320 billion from mid-August through the end of September. However, much of that advance has since been wiped out.

A broad rebound had lifted most assets listed on Binance, and in mid-August, 82% of those altcoins sat below their 200-day moving average. By early October the figure had dropped to just 10%, as such, nearly 90% traded above the long-term technical level and pointed to improving momentum.

That strength reversed as macroeconomic and political conditions worsened, and geopolitical and trade tensions remained elevated. Notably, the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, and the Bank of England all raised interest rates.

Additionally, midterm election results saw Democrats lose both chambers of Congress, thus adding further uncertainty.

Meanwhile, Equity markets witnessed a massive sell-off, with technology shares hit hardest. Former President Donald Trump linked the decline to the election outcome. The Nasdaq has fallen 14% from its recent peak, compared with a 6% drop for the S&P 500.

Altcoins suffered in the risk-off move as their total market capitalization declined by roughly $200 billion, erasing nearly two-thirds of the earlier gains. On Binance, about 70% of altcoins now trade below the 200-day moving average, a level approaching the 80% seen earlier and underscoring broad weakness.

The shift from the early October picture has been rapid, turning a widespread rally into a correction across most of the sector. Extreme readings of this kind have at times marked turning points in the past.

At report time, CoinMarketCap’s Altcoin Season Index currently stands at 38. The reading means 38% of the top 100 altcoins have outperformed Bitcoin over the past 90 days. This sits well below the 75 threshold that signals altcoin season and above the 25 level associated with Bitcoin season, reflecting a mixed market still tilted toward Bitcoin leadership.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

#5272. Ripple Prime Head Marc Asch to Step Down by the End of 2026

The Head of Ripple Prime, Marc Asch, is stepping down from the company by the end of 2015, according to a CoinDesk report citing a Ripple spokesperson.

Noel Kimmel, currently a Senior Vice President at Ripple Prime, will replace him in that role.

Ripple Prime was officially introduced after Ripple acquired Hidden Road in October 2025 for $1.25 billion, rebranding the latter.

Marc Asch founded Hidden Road in 2018 as a prime brokerage for institutional clients. Before that, Asch worked at SAC Capital.

Ripple Prime focused on institutional investment across several classes, including digital assets. Through Ripple Prime, the company also created new exposure to its native stablecoin, RLUSD.

That same month, Ripple also completed another $1 billion acquisition of a stablecoin platform, GTreasury, adding to its renewed financial ecosystem.

Recently, Ripple Prime has won the Prime Broker of the Year: EMEA award at the 2026 Hedgeweek US Awards.

The Hedgeweek US Awards is an annual event that honors and recognizes companies for their efficiency and contributions across several categories.

Some of these categories include custody, trading infrastructure, blockchain technology, compliance, and decentralized finance (DeFi).

The award has marked growing recognition of Ripple as a top brokerage firm in the world of finance.

#5271. ADA, XRP, DOGE: Gemini Names Biggest Losers of 2026

Crypto exchange Gemini has unveiled the biggest losers in the altcoin space for 2026 so far, as many of the crypto world's biggest digital currencies have been seeing massive double-digit price plunges.

Crypto exchange Gemini recently shared a list of 10 cryptocurrencies that have seen particularly brutal losses since the start of 2026 in a post on the X social media platform.

Topping Gemini's list of the biggest losers for this year is Bitcoin Cash (BCH), which has crashed a shocking 61.76% year-to-date.

Coming in second is Polkadot (DOT), with a 53.03% price decline, while Cardano (ADA) holds third place after shedding 48.04% of its value.

Ripple-related XRP and the top meme cryptocurrency Dogecoin (DOGE) are next in line, with losses of 43.43% and 42.38%, respectively.

Several other major cryptocurrencies are also seeing considerable losses, such as Sui (SUI), which has fallen 42.08%, Hedera (HBAR), which has dropped 38.13%, Solana (SOL), down 34.02%, Avalanche (AVAX), which has lost 33.40%, and Kaspa (KAS), which has gone down 30.75%.

Declining liquidity in the market, weakening speculative interest, lackluster institutional interest and general macroeconomic conditions are all major factors causing most major altcoins to underperform so far.

But for some, other issues within their ecosystems are also proving troublesome.

For instance, in the case of Cardano, the platform is seeing limited decentralized finance activity. As of Nov. 9, the total value locked in its DeFi ecosystem reportedly dropped below $50 million.

While Ripple continues its expansion in the institutional payments sector, stablecoin and tokenization areas, this hasn't necessarily led to sustained buying interest in XRP.

In fact, spot trading volume for XRP fell 53.5%, while perpetual futures trading volume dropped 44%.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, has been contending with waning speculative interest in meme cryptocurrencies.

Its institutional investment narrative also hasn't really caught on yet, with Bitwise announcing in September the shutdown of its Dogecoin ETF as the product failed to draw investor interest.

Bitcoin Cash has been seeing particularly sharp declines as it is now experiencing a reversal of its stellar 2025 performance, when the cryptocurrency soared around 38%.

Selling pressure picked up in May and June 2026 as BCH saw back-to-back monthly drops of over 30%.

A rebound could be seen in September after CME Group announced Bitcoin Cash futures, but this proved insufficient to stop the ongoing downtrend.

#5270. Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

BTC slips as Nvidia sinks 9% after hours and MSCI drops Strategy. ETFs lost $1.88B in November, 94% of it from IBIT.

In Bitcoin news, the coin fell from $74,811 to $73,480 within two hours of the U.S. close. Bitcoin slipped overnight after two shocks hit U.S. markets after Wednesday’s close. Nvidia shares fell about 9% in after-hours trading on a new report about CEO Jensen Huang. Index provider MSCI also confirmed it will remove Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, from its global indexes.

It trades at $73,588 on Binance on Thursday morning, down 0.4% in 24 hours and 5.8% in a week.

The funds are not helping. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) lost $299.8 million on Wednesday, their fifth straight day of outflows. Nasdaq futures are down 0.9%.

Bitcoin ETFs Shed $300 Million, Ether Funds Lose $145 Million

According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $300 million in net outflows on November 11, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT led individual fund inflows with $8.96 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $145 million in… pic.twitter.com/5sn88B2JQX

— Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain) November 12, 2026

So what happened, and how much of the selling comes from the ETFs?

The first hit came from Nvidia, the world’s most valuable chipmaker. The New York Times reported on Wednesday evening that Huang had a second relationship with a senior employee who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to remove him as CEO.

Nvidia had closed the day up 2.9% at $173.73. Within two hours, it traded at $157.99, down 9.1%. It is still down 8.6% before Thursday’s open. Nvidia has lost about 15% since last Friday. It first fell on Monday, after its board opened a separate probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Bitcoin has traded closely with tech stocks this year, and it fell with them. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 1.1% in the same two hours.

The second hit is closer to crypto. MSCI, whose indexes guide trillions of dollars in index funds, will delete Strategy from its global indexes after the market close on November 30. It ruled that Strategy looks more like an investment fund holding Bitcoin than an operating business. Japan’s Metaplanet and Upexi are also being removed.

Funds that track those indexes will have to sell their Strategy shares. JPMorgan earlier estimated that selling at about $2.8 billion. Strategy says the funds hold about 13 million shares, 3.1% of its stock. Its shares are down 1.8% before the open.

For Bitcoin news, that matters beyond one stock. Strategy is the steadiest corporate buyer of Bitcoin. Fewer index buyers for its shares could make it harder and more costly to raise money for new purchases.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

The ETF selling started before either shock. To see how big the ETF side of this Bitcoin news is, we added up the daily net flows of the U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs for every trading day in November.

The streak is not a record yet. The longest run of outflows this year lasted 13 trading days in May and June, just before Bitcoin fell below $60,000.

The Fed adds to the pressure. October’s hot inflation report on Tuesday pushed the odds of a December rate hike on Polymarket to about 97%. Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money out of funds like these.

BTC trades at $73,588, holding above Tuesday’s low of $72,727, its lowest price since August 20. On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, it sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,696 and the 200-day EMA at $76,422.

The next Bitcoin news to watch is Thursday’s ETF flow data and how Nvidia trades at the open. A sixth day of outflows and a weak tech session would put $72,727 to the test.

#5269. Rothschild Investment Reveals XRP ETF Stake

Rothschild Investment LLC, the Chicago-based investment management firm, has filed its latest 13F with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), revealing its stake in the Bitwise XRP ETF.

Rothschild Investment’s filing, made on Nov. 10, indicates that the company has invested in 6,300 shares of the Bitwise XRP ETF.

Based on the information provided, these shares were worth $104,769 as of Sept. 30.

The investment in the Bitwise XRP ETF is listed under CUSIP 09174F107 in Rothschild Investment’s third-quarter report.

Interestingly, Rothschild Investment did not have any reported holdings of the XRP ETF in its previous quarterly filing, which indicates that the firm’s investment in the XRP ETF occurred in the third quarter of 2026.

The Bitwise XRP ETF, listed under the ticker XRP, was introduced in November 2025.

The ETF enables traditional investors to invest in the Ripple-linked cryptocurrency without needing to buy and hold XRP tokens themselves.

Although Rothschild Investment has invested in the XRP ETF, it is not a significant part of its overall portfolio.

The firm’s total portfolio value for 13F-reportable holdings is around $2.69 billion.

Rothschild Investment holds much larger stakes in Bitcoin and Ethereum investments.

When it comes to cryptocurrencies, Rothschild Investment’s largest holding is in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF by BlackRock, where the company owns 40,188 shares worth around $1.9 million.

Additionally, Rothschild Investment reported holding $911,300 in the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust ETF and $335,160 in the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust ETF.

Other Bitcoin-related investments include the Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ETF ($125,113), VanEck Bitcoin ETF ($118,100), Bitwise Bitcoin ETF ($116,802) and Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund ($2,107).

In total, the seven Bitcoin investments represent around $3.51 million in reported holdings.

Rothschild Investment also has stakes in the Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF worth $538,622 and the Bitwise Ethereum ETF worth $476,500.

The company also has a significant holding in the Bitwise Crypto Industry Innovators ETF, with 24,250 shares worth $615,223.

The firm owns $38,360 worth of shares in the Grayscale CoinDesk Crypto 5 ETF.

Finally, it has invested $69,900 in a Solana ETF.

Aside from cryptocurrency investment funds, Rothschild Investment has shares in publicly traded companies that are heavily involved in the digital asset space.

Michael Saylor’s Strategy is one such holding, with a $530,763 investment.

Other holdings include Coinbase Global ($86,681), Block ($125,060) and Riot Platforms ($42,980), a Bitcoin mining company.

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast told reporters on Thursday, as reported by CNBC. The Florida Republican said lawmakers are still negotiating the exact date. The session is expected to involve several committees and will likely be held under oath with a transcript. Mast said he had told Huang he would issue a subpoena if needed. He also said Congress may hold public hearings with other people involved later. The testimony is expected to focus on Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, whom US officials reportedly believe passed information to China, and on whether Nvidia chips reached China through Megaspeed in breach of export controls. The announcement came hours after Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO, president and board member with immediate effect.

Chainlink sees a death cross approaching on the chart, with a solid possibility of an aggravation of the current state of affairs on the market. LINK is trading at around $10.49 at the moment, moving below every moving average on the daily chart.

The asset has already lost roughly a third of its value since the late September peak near $15.70, when the rally essentially ran out of steam.

The 50 EMA is rapidly diving down and most likely to cross the 100 EMA sooner rather than later. The 50 EMA sits near $11.70 right now, while the 100 EMA is around $11.40, so the gap between them is getting thin.

EMAs are also converging – an important sign that might cause some worrying certainly. The longest moving average on the chart, at around $11, was lost in early November, and LINK hasn't been able to get back above it since.

Luckily, volume is descending, so there's a good chance that things will stabilize rather than degrade from here. Daily volume in November is visibly lower than during the sell-off at the end of October, which is a good sign.

RSI is moving sideways, in a tunnel around 50, so the situation is, in some sense, neutral for the asset. The indicator hasn't made any sharp moves since mid-October, and the market isn't anywhere near the oversold zone.

Fundamentally speaking, Link also had a strong catalyst: Charles Schwab announced it will add LINK to its crypto trading platform, on par with Solana and Avalanche. The news came out on August 27, but LINK is now trading lower than it was on that day. For now, the closest support is the $10 price threshold, where buyers already stepped in twice over the last two weeks. If the death cross gets confirmed and $10 breaks, the drop most likely won't stop there, unfortunately.

Cardano continues the prolonged downtrend, with a possibility of plunging even lower in the foreseeable future. A strong uptick in volume here would be beneficial. Daily volume in November is among the lowest on the chart, so buyers aren't really showing up even at these prices.

The lack of catalyst is the larger problem: ADA has no traction around it and there's certainly a chance that it won't appear in the foreseeable future.

Fundamentally, ADA had no breakthroughs recently apart from the foundation's support of Cosmos IBC transition to Linux Foundation governance. It's more of an interoperability and institutional infrastructure related development.

Surprisingly, the first batch of wallets have already been developed, manufactured and ready to be sent out to the first owners. However, the Sui Foundation decided to play it safe and avoid potential issues with those who might want to reverse-engineer the wallet or plant a backdoor somewhere along the supply chain.

#5257. Bitcoin Crash Coming? Analyst Revisits 2014, 2018, and 2022 Pattern Ahead Of Midterm Elections

Bitcoin (BTC) could face another significant correction as the November 3 U.S. midterm elections approach, with analysts pointing to a historical pattern that has coincided with major BTC price declines during previous election cycles.

With the 2026 midterm elections just days away, market observers are examining Bitcoin’s performance around the 2014, 2018, and 2022 elections to see whether another downturn is approaching.

Although the historical similarities do not establish that elections directly influence cryptocurrency prices, the repeated appearance of major corrections during these periods has raised questions about Bitcoin’s near-term direction.

According to crypto analytics platform Alphractal, Bitcoin was already experiencing bearish conditions before each of the previous three midterm elections. However, selling pressure continued after Election Day, with the cryptocurrency eventually reaching significant cycle lows.

Looking back at the 2014 U.S. midterm elections held on November 4, Bitcoin was already caught in an extended bear market. The cryptocurrency continued declining in the weeks that followed, eventually reaching its cycle bottom in January 2015.

A similar development occurred in 2018. Bitcoin was trading around $6,400 when Americans headed to the polls on November 6. Although the market initially experienced a period of relative stability, BTC subsequently suffered a sharp decline, losing approximately 40% over the following month before establishing its cycle bottom in December.

Meanwhile, during the 2022 election cycle, Bitcoin had already experienced considerable losses by the time the November 8 elections took place. The collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX occurred around the same period, triggering another wave of selling that pushed BTC toward $15,500 and marked the bottom of that market cycle.

According to Alphractal, these three occurrences raise an interesting question about whether Bitcoin’s performance has any meaningful relationship with the U.S. electoral calendar.

The analytics platform emphasized that Bitcoin was already in a bear market ahead of all three elections. Consequently, the subsequent declines could have reflected broader cryptocurrency market conditions and the asset’s four-year cycle rather than the elections themselves.

Additionally, popular analyst Ali Martinez highlighted Bitcoin’s historical performance across four U.S. midterm election cycles.

According to Martinez, BTC recorded significant declines around the 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022 midterm elections, with reported losses of 72%, 65%, 52%, and 27%, respectively.

The analyst considers this repeated downside performance a pattern worth monitoring as another election approaches on November 3.

Furthermore, Martinez pointed to Bitcoin’s fourth-quarter returns during previous midterm election years. His figures show that BTC gained 391% in the fourth quarter of 2010, while the cryptocurrency recorded losses of 16.70% in 2014, 42.16% in 2018, and 14.75% in 2022.

The figures suggest that three of the four election-year fourth quarters ended negatively. However, the 2010 rally stands out as an exception, particularly because Bitcoin was still in its early stages of development.

For the upcoming election, Martinez identified $73,000 as an important price level to watch. He pointed to Bitcoin’s short-term holder cost basis, which represents the average acquisition price of coins held by relatively recent market participants.

According to his assessment, this level could become an important support area if selling pressure increases following the elections. A recovery from that region would potentially strengthen the bullish outlook, while continued weakness could signal further deterioration in market conditions.

Beyond the historical election pattern, technical analyst Crypto Patel has also raised concerns about Bitcoin’s immediate price direction, suggesting another substantial decline is possible.

In a recent market update, the pundit said Bitcoin had already fallen about 12% from his previously identified short-entry area. He explained that his bearish outlook originated from technical chart analysis rather than negative headlines or developments affecting the cryptocurrency industry.

The analyst based his assessment on Smart Money Concepts (SMC), which examines market structure, liquidity movements, and price action to identify potential trading opportunities.

Notably, Patel explained that Bitcoin’s price structure had produced a higher high, leading him to anticipate a subsequent move toward a higher low. He also highlighted the removal of inducement liquidity and a higher-timeframe candle closing below the relevant inducement level as additional bearish signals.

Regarding his latest projections, he identified $66,000 to $62,000 as his potential downside target, provided Bitcoin remains below $81,950.

However, the analyst also established a level that would invalidate his short-term bearish outlook. According to Patel, a higher-timeframe candle closing above $84,870 would prompt him to reconsider his position and return to a bullish stance, with expectations of a move beyond $100,000.

These projections suggest that Bitcoin could experience additional volatility as traders assess the market’s technical structure alongside the approaching U.S. elections.

At press time, BTC was trading at $71,454, down 3.92% over the past 24 hours.
