Nomura Holdings, one of Japan’s largest financial services companies, is reportedly considering selling its cryptocurrency subsidiary, Laser Digital, amid continued financial losses in its European operations.

According to Bloomberg, Nomura has held discussions with potential buyers, including financial services firm Marex Group. However, the company has not made a final decision yet and could still choose to retain the business.

This followed Nomura’s European operations reporting a pretax loss of 7.4 billion yen ($46.5 million) in the third quarter of 2026, marking their fourth consecutive quarterly loss. However, it’s not yet confirmed by Nomura whether Laser Digital was responsible for any part of the financial setback.

For background, Laser Digital was established in 2022 and provides institutional crypto trading, asset management, and investment services. Despite the possibility of a sale, the subsidiary has continued expanding its operations.

In fact, in August 2026, Laser Digital Japan secured the country’s first new crypto exchange registration in approximately four years, allowing it to offer institutional trading and liquidity services.

It also received preliminary approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in May to establish a national trust bank.

But it looks like market volatility and financial pressures may have prompted the company to reconsider its investment.

This is because the global crypto market’s trading volume has fallen to $64.513B after a drop of 21.3% in the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index also stood at 28 in the ‘Fear’ zone at press time.

At the same time, Japan’s latest inflation data has increased expectations that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) could raise interest rates again in December, potentially creating volatility across global financial markets.

This prediction comes as the producer prices rose 7.1% in October, exceeding economists’ expectations of 6.5%.

Import prices also surged 24.8% in yen terms, largely because the weak Japanese currency has made imported fuel, raw materials and other goods more expensive.

That said, another hike in December would mark the first time since 1989 that the country has raised interest rates three times in one calendar year.

This followed the United States’ reportedly joining Japan in supporting the yen through a coordinated foreign exchange intervention, marking its first such involvement since 1998.

Needless to say, the potential rate increase could also affect Bitcoin [BTC] and US stocks through the yen carry trade. Now, though, Japan has an estimated 5 million cryptocurrency owners, but its crypto adoption remains relatively limited.

This coincided with a recent report by AMBCrypto, wherein Japan’s major banking groups, including MUFG, SMBC, and Mizuho, are exploring yen stablecoins and cross-border payments.

Both demand components remain negative, leaving Bitcoin’s tentative stabilization dependent on persistent spot improvement and easing futures weakness.

Bitcoin’s improving spot-demand signal is losing ground to a sharper deterioration in perpetual futures. With the price near $73,000, that split leaves its attempted recovery vulnerable ahead of Friday’s US producer-inflation release.

Bitcoin traded around $73,478 at about 10:40 UTC on November 12. A Coinbase quote one minute earlier was about $73,469.

In a November 11 CryptoQuant note, analyst RugaResearch put the combined 30-day spot-and-perpetual demand estimate at negative 348,000 BTC on November 10, its weakest reading that month.

From November 7 to November 10, the spot proxy improved by approximately 29,500 BTC. The perpetual-futures estimate deteriorated by about 63,500 BTC over the same period. Both components remained below zero, leaving the improvement short of positive readings.

RugaResearch’s November 10 snapshot shows opposing three-day changes inside a still-negative 30-day demand estimate.

Perpetual deterioration was more than twice the spot improvement; both component levels remained negative.

Each reading adds a day and drops the oldest. That rolling window makes persistence across several closes more informative than one improvement.

This breakdown also differs from the apparent-demand measure discussed in CryptoSlate’s November 11 coverage. That article’s negative 284,000-BTC reading cannot be compared with negative 348,000 BTC as though one followed the other in a single series.

RugaResearch said spot moving toward zero, easing futures weakness and a flattening total while price holds its lows would strengthen the range case.

A separate CryptoQuant note by CoinNiel reported approximately 9,956 BTC in net exchange inflows on November 10, followed by about 981 BTC in preliminary net outflows on November 11.

CoinNiel labeled the November 11 data preliminary. Exchange withdrawals do not necessarily represent purchases, nor deposits sales, so several days of consistent flows would offer a stronger signal than one reversal.

The same note reported an all-exchange funding rate of 0.0051% in preliminary November 11 data, down from 0.0113%. Longs were still paying shorts, but at a lower reported rate.

In CoinNiel’s November 11 snapshot, open interest rose 1.2% from the previous day to about $26 billion, close to its seven-day average through November 10. That combination indicates lower long funding costs alongside slightly higher outstanding exposure. Open interest includes long and short positions, so its increase does not identify which side is driving the demand split.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs supplied a separate caution. Farside’s latest completed row showed net outflows of $300 million on November 11. Smaller withdrawals or sustained inflows would strengthen the stabilization case, but the latest reading still points to withdrawals.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics schedules October’s Producer Price Index (PPI) for Friday, November 13, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, or 13:30 UTC.

Inflation matters because it can change expectations for financing conditions. In his November 10 speech, delivered before that day’s consumer-inflation release, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said inflation remained too high and leaned toward a quarter-point December rate increase under his expected inflation path. That was his conditional view, rather than a commitment by the Federal Open Market Committee.

A PPI report that reinforces expectations of tighter policy could keep financing conditions restrictive and weigh on risk appetite. A softer report could ease that pressure.

Friday’s initial price reaction will leave the persistence test open. Renewed spot weakness or an accelerating futures drag would undermine stabilization, even if Bitcoin briefly rebounds after the release. Smaller ETF outflows and sustained exchange withdrawals would add context without replacing the component readings.

#5206. USDC Enters Dual EU Supervision as EBA Oversight Takes Effect

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: USDC’s European supervision changes on November 12, with the EBA and France’s ACPR sharing responsibilities.

USDC’s European regulatory status moves from an announced designation to an operating supervisory arrangement on November 12. That is the date set in the European Banking Authority’s October decision, which classified Circle’s dollar token as the EU’s first significant e-money token under MiCA.

NewsBTC covered the original significant-token designation last month. The development now is the scheduled transfer of specified responsibilities, making this a practical test of how the EU supervises a widely used stablecoin across agencies.

The EBA takes direct responsibility for own funds, reserves, liquidity requirements, and recovery and redemption plans. France’s Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution remains responsible for areas including governance, outsourcing, conflicts of interest and assessments of key personnel.

Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS is the relevant European issuing entity. The arrangement therefore divides duties between supervisors rather than replacing French oversight altogether. For anyone assessing a stablecoin provider, identifying the responsible legal entity remains part of understanding the regulatory framework.

The EBA’s explanation of its MiCA role says significant tokens face additional requirements because of the greater risks they may pose. Its framework combines assessments of significance, direct supervisory tasks and cooperation with national authorities.

For significant e-money tokens issued by electronic money institutions, the EBA focuses mainly on the additional liquidity and own-funds requirements. It also establishes and chairs a supervisory college to support cooperation and information sharing. The framework includes ongoing supervision away from the issuer’s premises alongside targeted on-site work.

Those functions address a different question from whether a token traded near one dollar yesterday. Reserves must support redemptions, and operational arrangements must hold up when conditions become less comfortable. A stable market price provides useful information, but it cannot show every weakness in an issuer’s processes.

An earlier EBA procedural decision describes powers that include requesting information, investigating, inspecting premises and taking supervisory measures. It also sets out how responsibility moves between authorities and how supervisory colleges are established.

That makes the milestone more substantial than an extra label. The significance of the transfer will emerge through continuing oversight and the issuer’s compliance with the applicable obligations. It is not a separate promise that every application using USDC will be secure or that every intermediary will process withdrawals without delay.

Consider a business receiving USDC through a payment processor. The issuer’s reserves, the processor’s handling of the transfer and the business’s own wallet controls are different parts of the transaction. Strengthening one part does not automatically validate the others.

Stablecoins are increasingly being considered within existing payment systems, including the Circle and ACI settlement work covered by NewsBTC. For a prospective user, a clear supervisory structure can make questions about accountability easier to direct.

The useful next questions concern how supervisory coordination works in practice, how the issuer explains its obligations and what public information becomes available about compliance. Businesses still need to assess their own service providers, contractual rights and operational arrangements.

November 12 establishes a defined oversight structure for a significant European stablecoin. Whether that structure delivers confidence over time will depend on its operation, especially when markets or payment systems come under pressure.

#5205. How will Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation affect crypto investors like you?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

When it rains, it pours. That’s how Nvidia investors feel right now.

The financial market had painstakingly priced in news of Nvidia’s President and CEO having an affair with a Chinese spy. Over the last 24 hours, however, it has been revealed that he also had a relationship with a junior executive at the company itself.

Simply put, sh*t hit the fan. And, NVDA’s performance highlighted that reality. At the time of writing, NVDA was trading at $164.23, down 14% in the last 5 days alone.

Thus, it was no surprise that Jensen Huang resigned. In a statement, the company’s board announced that CFO Colette Kress will take over as Interim CEO until a more permanent hire is made. The statement added,

Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.

Now that the resignation is past us, it’s worth taking a stock of the situation. To be specific, what does his resignation mean for the crypto sector?

The most immediate risk is one of spill-offs. Market analysts often see tech stocks, especially high-growth ones, and crypto as correlated risk-on assets. Thanks to the AI boom, Nvidia now accounts for 8% of the NASDAQ 100 and 7% of the S&P 500. This mean that any volatility in NVDA’s figures, significant or not, will have some impact on broader tech indices.

This impact is likely to extend to the crypto market as well, with fund managers likely to sell liquid assets like Bitcoin to raise cash or meet margin requirements if institutions see heavy losses in the tech sector.

This seemed to be the case at press time too, with the world’s largest cryptocurrency’s price hitting its lowest level on the charts in months. A hotter than expected U.S CPI weighed on the crypto market too.

That’s not all either. Publicly-traded Bitcoin miners like IREN and Core Scientific could also face new restrictions as far as their recent pivot to AI-driven HPC hosting is concerned. This is a pivot that has gathered steam over the last few years as Bitcoin mining became increasingly unprofitable, one driven by Nvidia’s GPU allocations and vendor financing.

Given what’s going on with the company, a new board with a new CEO might just play it safe and act cautiously. Especially until the leadership void is filled. This will affect not just borrowing costs for the aforementioned miners, but it could also increase underwriting risks. For instance, Christopher Brown, Senior Vice President for Investments at Synovus Securities, told Reuters,

Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.

This leadership void is a major issue. Not just for the company, but for any sector or market this company will affect too. In fact, this is a concern market analysts have already shared over the past few days. This was a sentiment shared by Australian fund manager Ten Cap’s Jun Bei Lu with Reuters,

There’s ​just a lot of uncertainty to come … not just for Nvidia; it’s for the whole AI — all the businesses that they co-invest and sponsor. I think ⁠the fear is that the music might stop.

Finally, there is the matter of individual cryptos in the market. Yes, the market as a whole will be affected, but it is also pretty evident that some will be more affected than others.  Especially since outside of what has been previously mentioned, the intersection of Nvidia with the crypto sector also includes cryptos linked to decentralized computing, GPU-backed infrastructure, and AI-linked assets.

These altcoins have often reacted to Nvidia-driven announcements and updates in the past, including keynotes and financial results. The significant sell-offs among these cryptos on the back of the Jensen Huang news means that resignations are a catalyst too. Except not a bullish one.

Just look at the likes of RENDER and NEAR, for instance.

RENDER’s price fell by over 11% in the 5 days after The New York Times report about Jensen and Alice Huang’s affair. At the time of writing, the crypto was bleeding fast as news of Huang’s resignation broke out.

Similarly, NEAR’s price has fallen by close to 30% since that report was first published. In the last 24 hours alone, NEAR was down by 9%, with its freefall on the charts likely to get worse as news of the resignation goes far and wide.

In many ways, it’s a little difficult to assess what will happen to Nvidia, the AI sector, and the crypto sector. Yes, there will be some volatility, but it’s the long-term that counts. A better indication would be to see how the market prices in and reacts to Nvidia’s financial results for Q3 2026. They are set to be released on 17th November.

A little more clarity on the leadership front and the future of the company’s commitments would be useful too.

#5204. XRP Risks Losing $1 Amid Aggressive $2.5 Billion Shift

As XRP continues to struggle amid the broad crypto market volatility while failing in multiple attempts to recover, key on-chain metrics are pointing to increased selling pressure among traders.

While momentum remains extremely weak, latest data from crypto analytics platform, Cryptoquant, shows that sellers have dominated both XRP’s spot and futures markets, putting it at risk of losing the long-held $1 mark.

Per the data, XRP’s cumulative volume delta (CVD) across major cryptocurrency exchanges shows that aggressive selling has dominated both its spot and futures market since September 23.

As of November 12, XRP’s Perpetual CVD on Binance has fallen from -$109 million to about -$1.1 billion. It is important to note that the CVD of an asset is a key metric that measures the difference between the volume of aggressive buy orders and aggressive sell orders over time.

While the metric turns negative when more traders are aggressively selling than buying, the -991 million negative balance in the Binance perpetual CVD signals stronger selling pressure.

With the negative balance on Binance exceeding its previous level by more than 10 times, this shows that traders have placed significantly more market sell orders than buy orders, either by opening short positions or closing existing long positions.

Apart from its futures market, further data shows that sellers have also dominated XRP’s spot activity across all major crypto exchanges, including Binance.

Notably, XRP’s All CEX Estimated Spot CVD moved from -$400 million to -$2.9 billion over the same period.

While this marks a $2.5 billion increase in the imbalance favoring sellers, it indicates that XRP spot traders have also been selling XRP more aggressively rather than buying, propelling the asset for further price declines.

#5203. Analyst Flags XLM Valuation Gap, Stellar Hits $4B

Home » Altcoins » Analyst Flags XLM Valuation Gap, Stellar Hits $4B

Stellar’s 6.1x growth in the RWA field paints a bright picture for XLM in the revamped financial ecosystem.

Stellar has released a new report from Allium Labs examining institutional activity on its network, showing rapid growth in tokenized real-world assets and stablecoin usage.

The findings arrive as technical analyst ChartNerd noted that XLM “is not priced in” pointing to a disconnect between on-chain institutional progress and the token’s market valuation.

According to the Allium report, Stellar’s tokenized asset market grew 6.1x to $4.12 billion over the 12 months through September 2026, compared with 2.3x growth across the wider market tracked by Allium. This lifted Stellar’s share of all tokenized RWAs from 4.9% to 12.7%.

$XLM is not priced in 🚀 https://t.co/vTs7eBJJGx pic.twitter.com/XfQEwD1O7l

Four new issuers – Spiko, Realiz, Tradable, and Ondo Finance – each now hold more than $500 million, joining Franklin Templeton among the network’s largest issuers. Spiko alone grew its assets on Stellar to $1.69 billion in under a year.

The network has become particularly dominant in one category: it holds 42% of tokenized non-U.S. government debt ($319 million of $766 million outstanding across blockchains as of September 2026), up from just 0.7% a year earlier.

Spiko’s Euro Treasury-bill fund accounts for the large majority of that total.

Stablecoin supply on Stellar rose 91% to $546 million over the same period. Adjusted stablecoin transfer volume reached $1.95 billion over the 12 months through September 2026, up 22%.

Business-to-business payments made up $1.34 billion of that volume (up 26%) and averaged $383 per transaction, far larger than the $15 average for consumer transfers.

The pattern indicates institutions are using the network for higher-value settlement rather than primarily retail activity.

The report includes examples of how established firms operate on the network. Franklin Templeton uses Stellar’s built-in controls to manage holders of its BENJI fund. MoneyGram enables customers to hold digital dollars and withdraw local cash.

A new report from @AlliumLabs digging into institutional finance on Stellar is out now.$4.1B in RWAs (now $5B+.) $319M in non-U.S. debt. 127% growth in stablecoin transfer volume.Plus case studies on @FTDA_US, @MoneyGram, @Spiko_finance, & more.https://t.co/6t2zMFzZ73

Other participants include Spiko and additional issuers that have scaled quickly after launching on the network. Protocol-native features such as holder approvals have been used at scale, with thousands of such actions recorded over the past year.

ChartNerd’s post that “XLM is not priced in” frames the institutional data against XLM’s current market position. The Allium figures show measurable expansion in tokenized assets, non-U.S. debt market share, and business-oriented stablecoin flows.

Whether these on-chain developments eventually narrow any perceived valuation gap depends on continued issuer growth, sustained payment volume, and broader market conditions.

#5202. Russia Sets November 22 Start for Exchange Crypto Trading, Subject to Approval

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Russian exchanges may begin cryptocurrency trading from November 22 if their trading rules receive the Bank of Russia’s concurrence. The November 11 announcement sets operating requirements for venues. A separate asset-eligibility ordinance takes effect on November 17, so the two dates describe different regulatory steps.

Russia has added another piece to its regulated crypto market framework, with a new ordinance setting the conditions under which exchanges can start trading digital currencies and digital rights. The Bank of Russia’s November 11 notice identifies November 22 as the earliest start under those rules, subject to the regulator agreeing to a venue’s trading arrangements.

That condition matters. An effective date creates a legal opening; it does not show that every exchange is technically ready or that every prospective customer can place an order on the same morning.

Under the announcement, exchanges must register trading participants, maintain records of orders and transactions, and monitor trading. They also have to calculate specified prices and report trading information to the central bank using the procedures applied to other assets.

These requirements address the organisation of a market: who participates, how activity is recorded and what the supervisor can inspect. The notice says the Ministry of Justice has registered the ordinance. It does not name a completed launch at a particular exchange or provide a forecast for trading volumes.

The central bank’s November 6 asset-eligibility announcement set a November 17 effective date for an ordinance covering Bitcoin, Ether and USDT. That notice deals with which assets non-qualified investors may access and the conditions attached to their purchases.

Non-qualified investors face an annual purchase ceiling of 300,000 rubles through a single intermediary. Qualified investors are not subject to that asset-list and purchase-limit restriction. The central bank says investors in both groups must pass the relevant test and familiarise themselves with crypto investment risks before transacting.

Reading the announcements together avoids a misleading single-date headline. One concerns the eligible assets and investor conditions; the other concerns organised trading requirements. Neither removes the need to check when a particular intermediary actually makes a service available.

A national regulatory opening can exist alongside changes at individual international exchanges. NewsBTC previously reported KuCoin’s withdrawal from Russia and Belarus, where affected users’ account notices determine their closure deadlines.

Those developments should be assessed separately. A domestic venue’s permission does not change another company’s service terms, and an international exchange exit does not by itself tell us when a domestic alternative will be usable.

For a trader, the practical questions include the identity of the intermediary, the assets it supports, how a purchase is funded and where holdings are kept. For an exchange, reliable records and price calculations become part of delivering a functioning service rather than merely announcing one.

The market impact depends on participation after services open. An expanded route into Bitcoin could bring additional buyers, but it could also shift activity from one channel to another. Permission alone cannot distinguish those outcomes or establish how much fresh capital will arrive.

There is a longer institutional backdrop. NewsBTC reported VTB’s conditional plans for direct crypto trading in December 2025. That historical proposal helps explain interest in domestic access, but it is not evidence that the bank has launched a service under the latest rules.

The next meaningful evidence from Russia will be venue-specific launch notices, completed onboarding and observable trading activity. Until those arrive, November 22 is best understood as a conditional regulatory starting point. It is a material step toward an organised market, with implementation still determining what customers can actually do.
